newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN sanctions panel defers talks on Iraq flights.
newsitem.headline: UN sanctions panel defers talks on Iraq flights.

text.p: The United Nations Iraq sanctions committee on Thursday deferred until early May discussion of controversial pilgrim flights which broke international flight restrictions, Western diplomats said.

Diplomats said after Thursday's session that, in an effort to put the current controversy behind it and avoid further breaches, next week's informal discussions will deal with future flights and not with those which already have taken place.
"This is so everyone can sound off a bit without taking up the time involved with a formal meeting," said a diplomat after Thursday's session.

Iraqi helicopters began arriving Tuesday at the Saudi Arabian border to ferry home pilgrims from haj observances in the Moslem holy city of Mecca, marking the second time in the past month that Baghdad flaunted restrictions on flights by its aircraft through the southern "no-fly zone."
The U.N. has banned international flights from Iraq since Baghdad troops invaded Kuwait in 1990.
Separately, the sanctions panel once again deferred a decision on granting Turkey an exemption on lifting estra Iraqi crude oil.

Since August, Turkey has asked the committee to allow oil imports above and beyond the oil-for-food accord's limits, claiming urgent economic need for such action due to billions in lost oil pipeline and other revenue since sanctions.
Sanctions panel members said it was too soon to act on the Turkish bid.

Diplomats said U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan will meet with Iraq's ambassador the U.N., Nizar Hamdoon, on Friday afternon to discuss delays in the distribution of food and medicines under the U.N. "oil-for-food" agreement, an exception to broader sanctions allowing Iraq to export up to $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for badly needed humanitarian goods.
The agreement comes up for renewable on June 10 but is widely expected to be renewed before that for another six months at the same level, diplomats said.
